events.label: birth
events.text: Born in Sutton Coldfield near Birmingham.

evidence.quote: Lucy Wills was born on 10 May 1888 in nearby Sutton Coldfield

events.text: Moved to Barnt Green south of Birmingham.

evidence.quote: and then from 1892 in Barnt Green to the south of the city

events.text: Went to Cheltenham school, a boarding school for girls in science.

evidence.quote: In September 1903 Wills went to Cheltenham

events.text: Passed Oxford Local Senior exam, Division I.

evidence.quote: She passed the Oxford Local Senior , Division I in 1905

events.text: Passed University of London Matriculation, Division II.

evidence.quote: the University of London , Matriculation , Division II in 1906

events.text: Began studies at Newnham College, Cambridge.

evidence.quote: In September 1907 , Wills began her studies at Newnham

events.text: Obtained Class 2 in Part 1 of Natural Sciences Tripos.

evidence.quote: obtained a Class 2 in Part 1 of the Natural Sciences Tripos in 1910

events.text: Finished her Newnham course.

evidence.quote: Wills finished her course in 1911

events.text: Obtained Class 2 in Part 2 (Botany) of Natural Sciences Tripos.

evidence.quote: Class 2 in Part 2 ( Botany ) in 1911

events.label: travel
events.text: Travelled with her mother to Ceylon.

evidence.quote: Later that year , Wills and her mother travelled to Ceylon

events.text: Published her first scientific paper, on plant cuticles.

evidence.quote: Willss first learned paper was in 1914 , on plant cuticles

events.label: travel
events.text: Travelled with brother Gordon to South Africa.

evidence.quote: In 1914 , she and her younger brother Gordon travelled to South Africa

events.text: Returned to England, arriving at Plymouth with Margot Hume.

evidence.quote: before she and Margot Hume returned to England , arriving in Plymouth in December

events.text: Enrolled at London School of Medicine for Women, Royal Free Hospital.

evidence.quote: In January 1915 , Wills enrolled at the London ( Royal Free Hospital ) School of Medicine for Women

events.text: Began research and teaching in pregnancy pathology dept, Royal Free.

evidence.quote: 1920 to 1928 . On qualifying , Wills decided to research and teach

events.text: Awarded Licentiate of the Royal College of Physicians, London (LRCP).

evidence.quote: Licentiate of the Royal College of Physicians London awarded in May 1920

events.text: Awarded University of London MB BS degrees.

evidence.quote: the University of London degrees of Bachelor of Medicine and Bachelor of Surgery awarded in December 1920

events.text: Research and teaching at Royal Free pathology department ended.

evidence.quote: 1920 to 1928 . On qualifying , Wills decided to research and teach

events.text: Began seminal research on macrocytic anaemia in India.

evidence.quote: In 1928 Wills began her seminal research work in India on macrocytic anaemia in pregnancy
Wills was in India between 1928 and 1933

events.text: Visited Mysuru.

evidence.quote: In 1929 she visited Mysuru

events.text: Working at Caste and Gosha Hospital, Madras.

events.text: Returned to Royal Free Hospital, London, full-time.

events.label: death
events.text: Died.

evidence.quote: Wills died on 26 April 1964

undated_mentions: late 1920s and early 1930s: research in India on anaemia (decade-level)
1911 to 1914: fragment after the Newnham paragraph, context unclear
two further papers in the 1920s, before India work
summers of 1930-32: returned to England for a few months
During the Second World War: full-time pathologist in the Emergency Medical Service
By the end of the war: in charge of pathology at Royal Free Hospital; established first haematology department
